title: EC2 Instance Fails Status Check (1/2 or 0/2)
symptom: AWS Management Console shows 'Status check failed' (1/2 or 0/2 checks passed) for an active EC2 instance.
initial_observations: System status check failed OR instance status check failed.
Instance may be unreachable via SSH and application traffic.
environment: EC2 instance running in AWS with attached EBS root volume.

possible_causes.cause: System Status Check failure (underlying AWS physical hardware/host problem)
possible_causes.remediation: Stop and then Start the EC2 instance (forces migration to a new healthy underlying physical host).

possible_causes.cause: Instance Status Check failure (guest OS kernel panic, corrupt filesystem, /etc/fstab error)
possible_causes.evidence_needed: InstanceStatus.Status == 'impaired'; console system log shows kernel panic or mount error.
possible_causes.remediation: Retrieve EC2 system log. If fstab/kernel corrupt, detach root volume, attach to rescue instance, fix fstab/grub, reattach.

investigation_steps.title: Query Specific Status Check State
investigation_steps.explanation: Distinguish between SystemStatus (AWS hardware) and InstanceStatus (guest OS).
investigation_steps.what_to_look_for: Look at SystemStatus.Status and InstanceStatus.Status fields.

investigation_steps.title: Retrieve EC2 Console Output (System Log)
investigation_steps.explanation: Inspect boot log for kernel panics, OOM conditions, or bad /etc/fstab entries.
investigation_steps.what_to_look_for: Look for 'Emergency mode', 'fsck failed', or 'Kernel panic'.

verification: After remediation, monitor `aws ec2 describe-instance-status` until both checks return 'passed'.
prevention: Configure CloudWatch alarm with EC2 auto-recovery action for System Status check failures.
Use 'nofail' mount options in /etc/fstab for non-root volumes.
